name: str_trunc
title: Truncate a string to maximum width

origin.description: Shorten a string so its length is at most width, marking the cut with an ellipsis.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: Maximum number of code points. It must be a single whole number, at least as long as the ellipsis.

arguments.name: side
arguments.text: Where the ellipsis sits: "right" (the default), "left", or "center". The whole word is required.

arguments.name: ellipsis
arguments.text: The text that replaces the removed part. The default is three dots.

origin.details: Length is the number of code points. A string that already fits is unchanged. A missing string stays missing. Width shorter than the ellipsis is an error.
origin.value: A character vector the same length as string.
origin.example:
x <- "This string is moderately long"
print(rbind(
  str_trunc(x, 20, "right"),
  str_trunc(x, 20, "left"),
  str_trunc(x, 20, "center")
))

translation.description: Shorten a string so its length is at most width, marking the cut with an ellipsis. The result is a list. A missing string is stringi._na.NA.
